bandwidth.title: Netlink Bandwidth Monitor
bandwidth.subtitle: The Netlink Bandwidth Monitor (nlbwmon) is a lightweight, efficient traffic accounting program keeping track of bandwidth usage per host and protocol.
bandwidth.notInstalledHint: The nlbw command was not found on the device. Install the nlbwmon package first.
bandwidth.configSubtitle: Accounting period, database and protocol mapping settings
bandwidth.restoreHint: Only archives generated by this page are accepted; they contain database files named YYYYMMDD.db.gz.
bandwidth.restoreMissing: Choose a backup archive to restore first
bandwidth.restoreOk: The following database files have been restored: {files}
bandwidth.downloadHint: Packs the databases of every accounting period into a tar.gz archive and downloads it.
bandwidth.forceReloadHint: Commits the temporary in-memory data to the database directory and reloads it.
bandwidth.kpiIpv6Share: of the total traffic is IPv6
bandwidth.configSaved: The bandwidth monitor configuration was saved
bandwidth.fPeriodHint: Choose "Day of month" to restart the accounting period monthly on a specific date, e.g. every 3rd. Choose "Fixed interval" to restart the accounting period exactly every N days, beginning at a given date.
bandwidth.periodWarning: Changing the accounting interval type will invalidate existing databases!
bandwidth.fDueDateHint: Day of month to restart the accounting period. Use negative values to count towards the end of month, e.g. "-5" to specify the 27th of July or the 24th of February.
bandwidth.dueDateMinus1: -1 - Restart every last day of month
bandwidth.dueDateMinus7: -7 - Restart a week before end of month
bandwidth.fStartDateHint: Start date of the first accounting period, e.g. begin of ISP contract.
bandwidth.fDaysHint: Length of accounting interval in days.
bandwidth.fIfacesHint: Only conntrack streams from or to any of these networks are counted.
bandwidth.noInterfaces: The device has no usable network interfaces yet.
bandwidth.fSubnetsHint: Only conntrack streams from or to any of these subnets are counted.
bandwidth.fLimitHint: The maximum amount of entries that should be put into the database, setting the limit to 0 will allow databases to grow indefinitely.
bandwidth.fPreallocHint: Whether to preallocate the maximum possible database size in memory. This is mainly useful for memory constrained systems which might not be able to satisfy memory allocation after longer uptime periods.
bandwidth.fCompressHint: Whether to gzip compress archive databases. Compressing the database files makes accessing old data slightly slower but helps to reduce storage requirements.
bandwidth.fGenerationsHint: Maximum number of accounting periods to keep, use zero to keep databases forever.
bandwidth.fCommitHint: Interval at which the temporary in-memory database is committed to the persistent database directory.
bandwidth.commit24h: 24h - least flash wear at the expense of data loss risk
bandwidth.commit12h: 12h - compromise between risk of data loss and flash wear
bandwidth.commit10m: 10m - frequent commits at the expense of flash wear
bandwidth.commit60s: 60s - commit minutely, useful for non-flash storage
bandwidth.fRefreshHint: Interval at which traffic counters of still established connections are refreshed from netlink information.
bandwidth.refresh30s: 30s - refresh twice per minute for reasonably current stats
bandwidth.refresh5m: 5m - rarely refresh to avoid frequently clearing conntrack counters
bandwidth.fDirectoryHint: Database storage directory. One file per accounting period will be placed into this directory.
bandwidth.protocolHint: Protocol mappings to distinguish traffic types per host, one mapping per line. The first value specifies the IP protocol, the second value the port number and the third column is the name of the mapped protocol.
